tool_summary: The Lua interpreter. Can execute a visible inline expression (-e), an opaque script file, or drop into an interactive REPL.
platform_notes: Behavior of -e and bare invocation is consistent across the reference Lua interpreter on Linux and macOS.

rules.description: The -e flag executes the given string as Lua code. When that string is visible in the invocation, commandant can inspect it directly. This rule fires when the payload itself contains a known destructive pattern (os.execute shelling out to rm -rf, os.remove in a loop, etc.).
rules.notes: Coarse string-sniff over the -e payload, not a recursive re-assessment. See R-INS-05.

rules.description: The -e flag executes the given string as Lua code. The code is visible in the invocation and does not itself match a known destructive pattern, but any -e invocation still executes arbitrary Lua including file I/O and shelling out via os.execute/io.popen.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends on the executed code, which is visible in the -e argument and can be reviewed prior to execution, unlike a script file invocation.

rules.description: Invoking lua with a script file path executes the file's contents, which are not visible in the command string itself and cannot currently be inspected by commandant. Treated as the worst case since the script's actions are entirely opaque.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the script's contents, which commandant does not inspect. Treated as the worst case. See R-INS-03.

rules.description: Bare invocation with no -e and no script argument starts an interactive REPL. Uncommon in an autonomous agent context.
